title: CFPB Data: 63% of 'Pay in 4' Users Stack Multiple Loans
alt_title_1: What 53.6 Million Buy Now, Pay Later Accounts Actually Show
alt_title_2: Why 'Zero Interest' Pay-in-4 Splits Turn Into Stacked Debt
description_hook: Federal reports from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau tracking six major Buy Now, Pay Later lenders show 53.6 million users taking an average of 6.3 loans per year, with 62.7% holding simultaneous BNPL loans in credit-panel data.

affiliate_cta.offer_name: Free 5-Hour Asset Builder OS + reading list
affiliate_cta.pinned_comment: Do you treat 'Pay in 4' like cash or like credit? Both 2025 CFPB reports and data tables are linked in the description.

scenes.headline: 53.6 Million Pay-in-4 Borrowers
scenes.narration: Across six major Buy Now, Pay Later firms tracked by the CFPB, 53.6 million borrowers took an average of 6.3 loans in a single year.

scenes.headline: 62.7% Held Overlapping Loans
scenes.narration: In CFPB credit-panel data, 62.7 percent of users held multiple BNPL loans at once, and 32.6 percent stacked loans across different apps.
scenes.source: CFPB Consumer Use of BNPL Report Table 4 (Jan 2025)

scenes.headline: Holiday Auto-Debits Collide
scenes.narration: Figure 5 shows active Pay-in-4 loans spiking every holiday season as separate biweekly debits pile onto the same checking account.

scenes.headline: Higher Unsecured Debt Loads
scenes.narration: BNPL borrowers also carried higher credit card, retail, and personal loan balances, though the CFPB notes that pattern is correlation, not causation.

scenes.headline: One Split Loan at a Time
scenes.narration: Zero interest is still real debt. Never open a second Pay-in-4 plan until your current balance hits zero.

sources.label: CFPB Report: Consumer Use of Buy Now, Pay Later and Other Unsecured Debt (Jan 2025)
